messages:
nora: Flagging a corner we missed: when a Private runtime loses control-plane for extended period, customers want predictable failure modes. Proposal: an "emergency-manifest" that is intentionally conservative and only permits a tiny surface (inference-only, no streaming, rate-limited).

kai: I like the conservative angle. Can we define explicit metric labels so observability can clearly distinguish emergency-serving vs normal-serving? Eg `redwood.serving.mode=emergency` and `redwood.manifest.version=sha256:...`.

oliver: +1 on metric labels. Also require a manifest checksum the runtime publishes so control plane can detect drift when it comes back. We should make the manifest immutable locally once active to avoid confusing ops.

sasha: Question: what about auth flows? If KMS passthrough is allowed in emergency, does the runtime temporarily cache wrapped keys? That has big security implications. I'd rather default to no key passthrough and require explicit customer opt-in with a signed acceptance token.

ops-bot: OpsBot: private/zone-e runtime 90c2 entered emergency-serving at 5212341012 (control-plane heartbeat lost). Manifest checksum: sha256:ab12...

elaine: Runbook must cover: 1) how to surface to customers (banner + SDK flag), 2) how we reconcile usage billing for emergency-serving, and 3) how support triages. Billing point: emergency mode should have distinct meter `emergency_inference_tokens` so finance can decide discounts.

nora: Good call on billing. For SDK behavior: return a small well-structured response when an unsupported feature is requested, not just an error code. Something like `{"code":"EMERGENCY_UNSUPPORTED","details":"function_calling_disabled","hint":"upgrade_to_dedicated_or_wait"}` so clients can retry/backoff appropriately.

kai: We also need a safety timeout: maximum emergency-serving window (eg 48h) after which the runtime must refuse requests unless an operator override is provided. That prevents indefinite drift. Document how to request overrides.

oliver: On the manifest schema: keep it tiny. Fields: mode, allowed_ops[], max_rps, manifest_version (sha256), acknowledgement_token (optional). Example:
```json
{"mode":"emergency","allowed_ops":["text_generate"],"max_rps":10,"manifest_version":"sha256:ab12..."}
```

Make `allowed_ops` explicit to avoid surprises.

sasha: Ops & Security note: if acknowledgement_token exists it must be signed by customer admin key and we need to log a proof-of-consent event. Also redact token in audit logs but keep presence boolean.

ops-bot: OpsBot: reminder - emit `redwood.alert.emergency_mode` metric with labels {runtime, manifest_version, duration_seconds}.

elaine: For rollout: canary in staging and one privacy-conscious customer with known SLAs. Also add an automated test that replays manifests and validates billing labels + error shapes.

nora: Action items: I'll write the short RFC with schema + example responses + runbook. @kai will add metric/telemetry spec. @oliver will add manifest immutability check in runtime. @sasha will draft the security consent flow. @elaine will coordinate billing label and canary list.

kai: I'll also add a Grafana dashboard tile for emergency-serving with the new labels.

oliver: I'll add a CI test that simulates control-plane flaps and verifies manifest checksum reconciliation on control-plane recovery.

sasha: And I'll work with legal on wording for the customer opt-in acceptance token.

nora: Thanks all — aiming to post RFC tomorrow for quick review.
